problem: The engineNote's proposed implementation does not work, and the note only hedges ("verify choiceGrants is honoured for skillChoices/redundantFallback"). I verified it: in build.ts the choiceGrants entry is merged via `for (const src of [g, fc.choice?.value ? g.choiceGrants?.[fc.choice.value] : undefined])`, and that loop applies ONLY armor / weapon / save / perception / skills / conditionalSkills. `skillChoices` is resolved outside that loop from the top-level grant only — `(g.skillChoices ?? []).forEach(...)` at build.ts:2151 — and `redundantFallback` is explicitly gated to the static grant by `if (g.redundantFallback && src === g && ...)`. weaponFamiliarity is the ONLY choice-dependent extra, handled in its own separate loop. So a choiceGrants entry containing `skillChoices` + `redundantFallback` would be silently ignored, and the style-dependent Acrobatics-or-style-skill option set cannot be expressed today.

Implementing this feat requires EITHER extending build.ts so choiceGrants entries also feed the skillChoices resolver (build.ts:2151) and the redundantFallback branch, OR a dedicated dependent-choice lane. Everything else in the spec is confirmed correct: the six options are exactly d.classes.swashbuckler.subclass.options (battledancer/braggart/fencer/gymnast/rascal/wit), the record has no `choice` field, and featGrantsAuto.ts:287 really is `'swashbuckler-dedication': { skillChoices: [{ options: 'any', rank: 'trained' }] }` (wrong — offers any skill). problem: The option source is wrong in a way that would match zero items: "content.items filtered to category 'weapon'". In core.json, weapons are identified by `itemType === 'weapon'` (1,039 records); `category` on a weapon item holds the PROFICIENCY tier — I counted simple 308 / martial 633 / advanced 71 / unarmed 6 / ammunition 3 — e.g. items['longsword'] is { itemType: 'weapon', category: 'martial', group: 'sword' }. There is also no `base` field on item records, so "keyed by base-item slug" is only true in the sense that the item id IS the slug.
correction: Filter `itemType === 'weapon'` and store the item id. That id is the right key: derive.ts builds each Strike with `base: w.id` and weaponMatches() tests `strike.base` against `critSpecWeapons.bases`, so the stored pick drops straight into the bases array. Everything else in this spec checks out and is the most valuable finding in the chunk: critSpecWeapons.bases really does contain the literal Foundry placeholder "{actor|flags.system.godlingWeapon}" (dead grant), StrikeDamageRider really has only appliesTo: 'all'|'unarmed'|'melee'|'ranged' (no per-base restriction), and weaponOverrides really is Record<weaponId, ProficiencyRank>, which is the right home for "treat this weapon as a simple weapon for proficiency".

problem: The engineNote's load-bearing claim is false: "zero items in core.json currently carry a choice or effectChoices field, so this would be the first item-driven builder prompt". 29 items already carry effectChoices — energy-robe, eidolon-cape, druids-crown, broadleaf-shield (x4), energy-resistant (x2), charm-of-resistance (x3), entertainers-cincture (x2), wyrms-wingspan (x3), wyrm-on-the-wing (x3), helm-of-zeal-greater, essence-charm, muse, track-of-the-beast, plus 4 aon-* duplicates. types.ts ItemBase documents the field: "'Choose one of N' passive effects (Energy Robe's resistance type)... resolved into resolvedItemPassives when worn". Item-choice wiring (ItemBase.effectChoices -> BuildState.effectChoices keyed <recordId>:<choiceId> -> resolvedItemPassives) already ships and needs no new plumbing. What is actually missing is three narrower things: (1) EffectChoice can express a fixed `options` list or an open `spellFilter`, but has no skill/Lore filter — a free-text-Lore analogue of spellFilter is the natural extension; (2) free-text Lore input already exists TWICE (Background.trainedLoreChoice -> BuildState.backgroundLore, and DefenseGrants.loreChoices -> BuildState.heritageLore) but both grant TRAINED, so the conditional master/legendary-at-15 rank override is the real new capability; (3) the 'a Lore you have no proficiency in' validator and the once-per-day re-pick (daily preparations) still need somewhere to live. The human question should therefore be only 'one-time invest prompt vs daily-prep slot, and enforce-or-warn' — not 'should items be allowed builder prompts at all'.

problem: needsEngineWork:false is wrong. problem: needsEngineWork:false with no engineNote at all is wrong, and the reasonIfNo's claim that Specialty Crafting's choice 'must be prompted there' asserts a prompt that does not happen. feats['specialty-crafting'].choice is present (flag 'specialtyCrafting', 12 options alchemy…woodworking), but as a background grantedFeatId it goes through build.ts:1900-1903 / Builder.tsx:990-1004, which never render a picker and never store a value. problem: The core finding (hardcoded trainedLore) is correct and confirmed — the record really does carry `"trainedLore": "Jungle"` with no trainedLoreChoice, so build.ts:1201 trains it unconditionally and 2 of 3 legal builds are unreachable. problem: The spec's structured fields encode ONLY the branch affiliation (flag magaambyanBranch, picks 1). The record's headline benefit is a different, unrecorded build-time choice: "You gain the ability to cast a single arcane or primal cantrip of your choice... If you weren't already, you become trained in that tradition's spell DCs and spell attack rolls, with Intelligence as your spellcasting ability if you choose arcane or Wisdom as your spellcasting ability if you choose primal." correction: Promote this to a MULTI-CHOICE record. (1) PRIMARY — tradition: kind 'array', flag 'halcyonTradition', options [{arcane → spellcastingGrant {tradition:'arcane', keyAbility:'int', proficiency:'trained'}}, {primal → {tradition:'primal', keyAbility:'wis', proficiency:'trained'}}]. Feat.spellcastingGrant is a fixed object, so the two options must each carry their own — that IS the engine gap to state. (2) DEPENDENT — cantrip: open pick, SpellChoiceFilter { traditions:[<chosen>], cantripsOnly:true, grantAs:'innate', innate:{ tradition:<chosen>, atWill:true, heightenHalfLevel:true } }; or, to avoid the dependent-pick gap entirely, ship it today as two FEAT_CANTRIP_GRANTS-style fixed lists (arcane cantrips / primal cantrips) the way arcane-tattoos and wildborn-magic already do. Also correct as the spec says: add conditionalRank {base:'trained', upgraded:'expert'} to FEAT_SKILL_GRANTS['magaambyan-attendant-dedication'].skillChoices (verified present in featGrants.ts:92 and used by build.ts:2158, and verified missing from featGrantsAuto.ts:188).

problem: Two errors. (a) needsEngineWork: true is wrong — no engine change is needed. The record can be fixed with data alone by the exact pattern additional-shadow-magic already ships: `effectChoices: [{ id:'school-spell', options: [8 × { value, label, grant:{ focusSpells:[<id>] } }] }]` AND deleting `focusPoolBonus: 1`. FeatChoiceDef (types.ts) is only { flag, prompt, kind:'domains'|'array', options } and an 'array' choice grants NOTHING — build.ts's applyFeatFocus only turns a choice into a focus spell when kind === 'domains' (line 1374). Authoring this as choice.kind 'array' would record a label and grant no spell.

Replace kind:'array' with an effectChoices spec (id 'school-spell', the same 8 options, each option's grant = { focusSpells: [id] }), and state explicitly that `focusPoolBonus: 1` must be REMOVED from the record in the same edit. Option ids verified present in core.json: protective-wards, fortify-summoning, diviners-sight, charming-push, force-bolt, warped-terrain, call-of-the-grave, physical-boost (the legacy slugs protective-ward / augment-summoning / charming-words are indeed absent). problem: The engineNote inverts the actual defect. It claims the top-level `innateSpells: [{spellId:'enlarge', tradition:'primal'}]` is applied IN ADDITION to the chosen option's grant, 'so this feat currently grants Enlarge TWICE'. It does not. build.ts pushes each taken feat's top-level innateSpells at lines 2536-2540, THEN the resolved effect-choice grants (chosenInnateGrants) at 2542-2545, and then dedupes by spellId keeping the FIRST occurrence: `const seenInnate = new Set<string>(); const innate = innateGrants.filter((g) => content.spells[g.spellId] && !seenInnate.has(g.spellId) && seenInnate.add(g.spellId));` (build.ts:2555-2556).
correction: The top-level grant SHADOWS the chosen one — the player's pick is completely inert, not duplicated. Whichever option is selected, the character ends up with a single generic Enlarge cast at its base rank 2 with the default 1/day (castRank at build.ts:2561-2568 sees no `rank`, and usesPerDay defaults to 1 at 2581). So enlarge-2nd loses its 2/day and enlarge-4th loses BOTH its rank-4 and its 1/day distinction. The fix (delete the top-level innateSpells now that effectChoices covers it) is unchanged, but the reported symptom must be 'the choice does nothing' — that is the Assurance failure mode, and it will not be found by looking for a duplicated Spells-page row.

problem: Three defects. problem: Says the record's effectChoices are complete ("Nothing to add", needsEngineWork false) and reports "16 options". problem: engineNote claims "the ten initiate-benefit-<implement> classFeature records exist in core.json but nothing in src/ references them". problem: engineNote says "NOT implemented anywhere … no BuildState field, no effectChoices on the record, and no code path mentions it" and proposes a hand-typed 3-option array, then claims "Blessed Swiftness is nearly expressible via DefenseGrants.landSpeedBonus: 5, except that field is a flat bonus while the text specifies a STATUS bonus". problem: The VERDICT is right (this is the one genuine build-time pick in the chunk: "When you first invest *The Queen Mother*, choose a Lore skill in which you have no proficiency" → master, legendary at 15th). But the engineNote is wrong on three load-bearing facts, and all three overstate how much new engine work this needs. (a) "zero items in core.json currently carry a choice or effectChoices field, so this would be the first item-driven builder prompt" — FALSE. 29 items carry `effectChoices` today (energy-robe, druids-crown, entertainers-cincture, broadleaf-shield x4, charm-of-resistance x3, wyrms-wingspan x3, eidolon-cape, essence-charm, energy-resistant x2, helm-of-zeal-greater, ancestral-geometry, …), and src/rules/build.ts already resolves inventory-item effectChoices (`resolvePick(inv.itemId, content.items[inv.itemId]?.effectChoices, …)`, ~line 2389) into item passives. Item-driven builder prompts are shipping, not unprecedented. (b) "There is no free-text/open Lore kind … the free-text Lore input built for backgrounds (BuildState.backgroundLore) is not reusable from an item" — misleading. A SECOND, more general free-text Lore lane already exists: `FeatGrant.loreChoices?: number` (src/rules/featGrants.ts:78), whose picks are typed by the player and stored in `BuildState.featLoreChoices` keyed `<featId>:<slot index>`, granted as `lore:<subject>`. (c) "EffectGrant.skills … with no level condition, so 'master, legendary at 15th' needs a conditional-rank grant" — the primitive already exists in the sibling lane as `FeatGrant.rankUpgrade` ({level, rank}, list form for multi-step ladders) and `FeatGrant.skillChoices[].conditionalRank`. Minor: the spec's own top-level `"kind":"open"` is not a legal value — FeatChoiceDef.kind is `'domains' | 'array'` only (the spec says so itself two sentences later).
correction: Keep needsBuildChoice true, chooses 'skill', picks 1, effect = set the chosen Lore's rank to master (legendary at 15th+) while invested. Rewrite the engineNote to: the missing piece is WIRING an existing free-text-Lore + level-conditional-rank grant to an ITEM, not inventing one. Concretely: (1) items already get builder prompts via `Item.effectChoices` → build.ts resolvePick, but that lane only accepts a fixed `options` enumeration and only yields `EffectGrant`, so a free-text Lore slot on an item is the new bit; (2) the free-text mechanism to copy is `FeatGrant.loreChoices` + `BuildState.featLoreChoices` (featGrants.ts:78), not `BuildState.backgroundLore`; (3) the level ladder to copy is `FeatGrant.rankUpgrade`; (4) still genuinely absent: the 'a Lore you have NO proficiency in' validator and the once-per-day re-pick during daily preparations (which belongs in play/daily-prep state, not the immutable build). needsHumanDecision stays true, but the question should be posed as 'reuse the item effectChoices lane with a new free-text-Lore choice kind, or hang it off a daily-prep slot?' — not 'should items be allowed to prompt at all'.

problem: The `effect` and `engineNote` overstate what exists. problem: The engineNote's supporting claim is false: "EffectGrant already supports halfLevel resistances — Deep Fetchling uses the same pattern". Its record is: choiceResistance: { options:[{cold},{void}], halfLevel:true } — a HERITAGE-ONLY field declared at src/rules/types.ts:492 (immediately above the Background interface at 495, which does not have it), consumed at builder/shared.tsx:2351, validated at build.ts:508 and applied at derive.ts:733. An implementer following the note would search deep-fetchling for effectChoices and find nothing.

Restate the engine path as: half-level resistance IS expressible through EffectGrant, but via an IwrEntry FORMULA VALUE — IwrEntry.value accepts a string like "max(1,floor(@actor.level/2))" (types.ts:236) resolved by resolveFormula (derive.ts:541, applied to resistances at derive.ts:690) — not via a halfLevel flag. Two viable paths, and the note should offer both: (a) generalize the existing heritage `choiceResistance` lane to Background — it is an exact shape match (options + halfLevel) and already carries a "you must pick" validator at build.ts:508 — or (b) add effectChoices to Background with each option's grant carrying resistances:[{type:<energy>,value:'max(1,floor(@actor.level/2))'}] plus skills:{'lore:<energy>':'trained'} pre-baked, which also solves the derived-Lore problem the spec correctly flags.

problem: The needsBuildChoice:false verdict is correct, but the engineNote is factually wrong about the senses half. It says "senses[] carries a flat low-light-vision" and frames the gap as only the missing conditional upgrade (Heritage's darkvisionIfAncestryLowLight). And deriveDefenses() (src/rules/derive.ts:619-667) builds its `sources` array from heritage, feats, class features, class-archetype features, worn items, active stance, active-state grants and chosenEffects — the background is never pushed as a source (grep for 'background' in derive.ts returns zero hits). So feral-child's `senses: [{low-light-vision}, {scent, range 30, imprecise}]` block is entirely DEAD DATA: neither sense reaches the sheet today, not just the darkvision upgrade.
correction: Restate the engineNote as: Background carries a `senses` array in core.json that nothing reads. Fix requires (a) `Background extends ContentBase, DefenseGrants` (or an explicit senses field) in types.ts AND (b) pushing the resolved background into deriveDefenses' `sources` list; only THEN does the conditional 'low-light, or darkvision if you already had low-light' rider (Heritage's darkvisionIfAncestryLowLight equivalent) become the remaining gap. Severity is higher than the spec implies — the imprecise scent 30 ft is silently lost too, not just the upgrade. The other half of the note (Survival dropped because trainedSkill only holds 'nature' and Background has no two-fixed-skills field) is confirmed correct.

problem: The proposed shape is wrong and would create a DUPLICATE prompt. The spec asks for a generic choice {flag:'divineAttribute', kind:'array', options:[6 attributes]}, but an attribute boost is not modelled by `choice` in this app — it is modelled by abilityBoosts. shared.tsx:2182 does `boostSlots(background.abilityBoosts)` and 2445-2453 renders one AbilitySelect per slot, so this record ALREADY renders two boost dropdowns. Adding a `choice` on top gives the player two free-boost pickers plus a third 'Divine attribute' picker for the same boost. Secondly, the `effect` is over-broad: it claims the choice 'Constrains boost #1 ... the deity's Divine Skill becomes the trained skill; Assurance is granted with that same skill; a deity Lore is trained.' Training the Divine Skill, pinning Assurance and training the deity Lore are three independent grants of the background — none of them is a consequence of picking the attribute.
correction: Drop the `choice` field entirely for this record. Model it as abilityBoosts[0] becoming a deity-derived constrained boost — a new AbilityBoost kind (e.g. {kind:'deityDivineAttribute'}) resolved against deities[build.deityId] at render time in boostSlots — so it reuses the existing single boost picker instead of adding a second one. Narrow `effect` to just 'constrains background boost #1 to the chosen deity's Divine Attribute'. Keep the (correct) separate findings as their own gaps: missing trainedSkill sourced from deities[deityId].skill, Assurance needing a pinned skill, and the divineAttribute data backfill. needsHumanDecision:true and the question are both correct and should stay.

problem: The engineNote is factually wrong about the engine. It claims the pre-set sub-choice of a background-granted feat is "neither prompted nor stored" and that the fix needs a new `Background.grantedFeatChoice?: string (or Record<flag,value>)` PLUS "a stable slot key for the background feat". The storage lane and the resolver already exist: `BuildState.grantedFeatChoices?: Record<featId, string>` (build.ts:193) is the app's established home for SLOTLESS granted feats' sub-choices, and buildCharacter already runs the BACKGROUND feat through it — build.ts:1417 `pushFocusBonus(resolveBackground(build, content)?.grantedFeatId)` → build.ts:1440 `applyFeatFocus(id, build.grantedFeatChoices?.[id])` → `grantedChoiceById[id]` (build.ts:1441). applyFeatFocus (build.ts:1365-1396) returns the resolved {value,label} for ANY feat with a `choice` def, not just focus feats.
correction: No slot key and no Record<flag,value> are needed. The only two real gaps are: (a) build.ts:1901 pushes the background feat as `{ featId, level: 1, category: 'skill' }` with no `choice:` — it should pass `choice: grantedChoiceById[background.grantedFeatId]`, exactly as the sibling pushes at build.ts:2053 / 2067 / 2074 do; (b) Builder.tsx:990-1004 renders the background feat read-only with no picker. For alloysmith specifically (a PINNED value, not a player pick) the one genuinely new piece of data is a Background field carrying the pinned value (e.g. `grantedFeatChoiceValue?: string` = 'blacksmithing') that seeds grantedFeatChoices['specialty-crafting']. The classification itself (needsBuildChoice: false, because the text dictates blacksmithing) is correct.

problem: Same wrong engineNote as alloysmith, and here it is wrong in a stronger way: it says the specialty "belongs to a background-GRANTED feat, and granted feats are never offered their sub-choice", and makes fixing it depend on alloysmith's proposed new Background field. problem: The engineNote says "There is no background-level spell picker. Both would be needed: add innateSpells?: InnateSpellGrant[] (or a chosen-spell variant) to Background plus a filtered cantrip picker in the Setup card." Both halves are wrong. An open, filtered spell picker already exists and ships: `EffectChoice.spellFilter` / `SpellChoiceFilter` (types.ts:380-412) with `grantAs: 'innate'` and `innate: Omit<InnateSpellGrant,'spellId'>`, resolved by `spellsMatching` / `grantForSpellPick` (src/rules/spellChoice.ts) and rendered by the builder at Builder.tsx:1288-1300+. And `Background.innateSpells` would be the WRONG field anyway, since the cantrip is CHOSEN, not fixed.
correction: The single real gap is that `Background` (types.ts:495) extends only ContentBase, while `effectChoices?: EffectChoice[]` lives on `DefenseGrants` (types.ts:304) which Feat/Heritage/ClassFeature extend. Minimal fix: let Background carry effectChoices, then express this record as one EffectChoice with `spellFilter: { traditions: ['occult'], cantripsOnly: true, grantAs: 'innate', innate: { tradition: 'occult', atWill: true, heightenHalfLevel: true } }` — all four of those InnateSpellGrant field names are real (types.ts:455-474). One genuine residual gap the spec missed and should name instead: `SpellChoiceFilter` has NO rarity field and `spellsMatching` performs no rarity check, so the text's "common" restriction cannot be enforced today. Classification (needsBuildChoice true, cantrip, 1 pick, empower riders in-play, [free, free] boosts) is correct.

problem: EngineNote gaps (1) and (2) are wrong as stated. It says the at-will primal cantrip "cannot be granted at all" and that "There is no linked/branching choice on Background", then proposes a bespoke `Background.elementChoice`-style branch. The engine already has a linked one-pick-two-grants construct: `EffectChoice.options[].grant: EffectGrant`, and EffectGrant carries BOTH `skills?: Partial<Record<ProficiencyKey, ProficiencyRank>>` and `innateSpells?: InnateSpellGrant[]` (types.ts:359-378). `ProficiencyKey = SkillId | \`lore:${string}\`` (types.ts), so a Lore is grantable through that same lane.
correction: No new branch type. Give Background the existing `effectChoices` lane and encode one EffectChoice with six options, each option's grant being e.g. `{ skills: { 'lore:plane-of-fire': 'trained' }, innateSpells: [{ spellId: 'ignition', tradition: 'primal', atWill: true }] }`. All six spell ids are confirmed present and rank 0 in core.json (gale-blast, scatter-scree, ignition, needle-darts, spout, root-reading). The spec's gap (3) is correct and must stay: the record's current `trainedLoreChoice: true` has to be REMOVED, otherwise the player free-types any Lore and gets no cantrip.

problem: The shared engineNote asserts "No field expresses 'a Lore from THIS fixed list'. Background has only trainedLore (fixed string) and trainedLoreChoice (boolean → free-text)", and proposes a new `trainedLoreOptions` field replicated across five records. The premise is only true of Background: the app's blessed "choose one of N, each option confers a concrete effect" lane already exists as `EffectChoice` + `EffectGrant.skills` (types.ts:299-304, 359-378), with `ProficiencyKey` accepting `lore:<subject>`, a builder picker, and BuildState.effectChoices keyed `<recordId>:<choiceId>`.
correction: State the gap accurately: Background does not extend DefenseGrants, so it cannot carry `effectChoices` — that ONE change covers all five of these Lore lists (plus elementally-infused and harrow-chosen) with zero bespoke fields; e.g. hammered-by-fate becomes options daemon/demon/devil each granting `skills: { 'lore:daemon': 'trained' }`. A dedicated `trainedLoreOptions` would be a simpler Setup-card render and is a legitimate design preference, but it should be presented as the owner's choice, not as "no field expresses this". The data facts in these five specs are all confirmed correct (hammered-by-fate hard-codes trainedLore 'Daemon', keys-to-destiny 'Art', concordance-scout and planar-migrant 'Plane of Air', conservator 'Accounting').

problem: EngineNote calls this "Worst-case of the Lore gap: needs BOTH a restricted option list AND MULTI-pick", proposing `trainedLoreOptions + trainedLorePicks?: number` with `BuildState.backgroundLores?: string[]`. The multi-pick part is not a gap: a record may carry an ARRAY of EffectChoices (`effectChoices?: EffectChoice[]`, types.ts:304), each with its own stable `id`, so four independent 6-option Lore choices are expressible with the existing lane once Background can carry effectChoices.
correction: Reduce the engineNote to the one thing that genuinely has no existing lane: nothing in EffectChoice can enforce that the four picks are DISTINCT (four separate choices would let a player take Plane of Air Lore four times). Either accept that, or the new field must add a distinctness constraint. Everything else in the spec is right, including that this background grants no ordinary skill and no skill feat (confirmed: the record has neither trainedSkill nor grantedFeatId) and that the current record trains a single malformed `lore:Plane of Air`.

problem: The second gap is described as "Background.grantedFeatId is a single string, so Prescient Planner is silently dropped. Would need grantedFeatIds?: string[] or similar." A multi-feat grant lane already exists: `grantsFeats?: string[]` on DefenseGrants (types.ts:262), applied in build.ts:2043-2056 for heritages, feats and invested items — including `choice: grantedChoiceById[gid]` for their sub-choices.
correction: Say that the fix is to expose the existing `grantsFeats` lane on Background (the same one-line change — Background gaining the DefenseGrants lanes — that solves the Lore, cantrip and linked-pick cases above), not to invent `grantedFeatIds`. The dropped feat itself is confirmed: the record has `grantedFeatId: 'hefty-hauler'` only, and `prescient-planner` exists in core.json. The choice classification (1 of 6 planar Lores) is correct.

problem: The engineNote asserts the Terrain Stalker grant is fine as-is: "the feat's own three-option choice (rubble/snow/underbrush) is correct and already works; do not narrow it." The 'already works' half is false, and it causes the spec to miss a second, real build-time choice. Background-granted feats are injected at src/rules/build.ts:1900-1902 as `feats.push({ featId: background.grantedFeatId, level: 1, category: 'skill' })` — no `choice` property is ever attached — and the ONLY granted-feat sub-choice picker in the builder (src/builder/Builder.tsx:1263-1285) is gated on `FEAT_FEAT_GRANTS[picked]`, i.e. feat-grants-another-feat. Nothing anywhere reads `background.grantedFeatId` to render a picker; the background card (src/builder/shared.tsx:2432-2433) only prints the feat's name. The round-trip at build.ts:3254-3257 drops the background feat entirely without preserving any choice. So a Hell-Hunted character gets Terrain Stalker with NO terrain — exactly the Assurance failure mode, on the feat rather than the background.
correction: Keep needsBuildChoice=true, but record TWO choices, not one. (1) The Lore pick as specced (devil/hellknight) — correct. (2) ADD a second choice: flag 'terrain', prompt 'Terrain', kind 'array', chooses 'terrain', picks 1, options rubble/snow/underbrush (the full unrestricted list from the terrain-stalker record, which carries `choice: { flag: 'choice', prompt: 'Prompt', kind: 'array', options: [rubble, snow, underbrush] }`), effect = sets the terrain in which you can Sneak without a Stealth check while undetected. Rewrite the engineNote: the terrain is currently UNCHOOSABLE, not merely unrestricted. The engine needs a background-granted-feat sub-choice lane — inject the feat with a resolved `choice` in build.ts:1900-1902 (mirroring the grantedChoiceFeats resolver at build.ts:1948-1959) and render a picker for it on the Background card, keyed into the existing `BuildState.grantedFeatChoices` map (build.ts:193, already read at build.ts:1440 and round-tripped at :3251).

problem: Two errors in the engineNote, both understating the gap. (1) It says "Without it the player can pick Snow, which this background forbids" — implying a prompt exists and is merely unrestricted. No prompt exists: as with hell-hunted, build.ts:1900-1902 injects the granted feat with no `choice`, and Builder.tsx:1263-1285 only renders sub-choice pickers for FEAT_FEAT_GRANTS ids. The player cannot pick Snow because the player cannot pick anything; Terrain Stalker arrives with no terrain at all. (2) It says "there is no field to restrict a granted feat's choice per grant. Needs something like `Background.grantedFeatChoice?: { flag: string; options: string[] }` (or a generic per-grant option filter…)" — that generic per-grant filter ALREADY EXISTS and is in production use, so the spec proposes inventing a field that duplicates one already in the codebase.
correction: Classification (needsBuildChoice=true, terrain, 1 pick, rubble/underbrush only, snow excluded) is right — keep it. Fix the engineNote on both points. (1) State that the terrain is currently unchooseable, not merely unrestricted, so this is the same missing-prompt bug as hell-hunted rather than a narrowing bug. (2) Reuse the existing restrict shape instead of inventing one: `grantedChoiceFeats?: { featId: string; restrictTo?: string[] }[]` is already defined on subclass/extra-choice options (src/rules/types.ts:633), resolved at src/rules/build.ts:1948-1959 (`const allowed = gcf.restrictTo?.length ? gcf.restrictTo : f.choice.options?.map(x => x.value) ?? []`, defaulting to the first allowed value), rendered by the picker at src/builder/shared.tsx:2600-2605 (which shows only when `restrictTo.length > 1`), and round-tripped via `build.grantedChoiceFeatTraits` (build.ts:3029-3031). The fix is to add the same `grantedChoiceFeats` field to `Background` (src/rules/types.ts:502-509) and point the existing resolver/picker at it — `{ featId: 'terrain-stalker', restrictTo: ['rubble','underbrush'] }` — not to define a new `Background.grantedFeatChoice`. The separate finding that the Hallit grant is unmodelled (`Background` has no language field; `bonusLanguageSlots()` at build.ts:740 counts only Int mod + ancestry extras) is confirmed and should stand as written.

problem: The choice block is malformed and the pick count is wrong. It declares kind 'array' with picks:2 but supplies a single option (Thassilonian) that is not optional at all — the text FORCES it. Verified feats['multilingual'] description: "You learn two new languages, chosen from common languages, uncommon languages, and any others you have access to. You learn an additional language if you are or become a master in Society and again if you are or become legendary." So (a) Thassilonian is a fixed grant, not an option; (b) the player's real build-time pick is ONE language from an open pool; (c) even that count is not static — it grows to 2 free picks at master Society and 3 at legendary, so any hardcoded picks number is wrong. The proposed new engine field is also a reinvention.
correction: Keep needsBuildChoice:true but restate as: chooses 'language', OPEN source = the core.json `languages` collection (120 entries, thassilonian confirmed present), picks = (Multilingual's language count) MINUS 1, with 'thassilonian' pre-assigned to the remaining slot. Do NOT emit a 1-item array. Engine note should point at the EXISTING lane instead of a new `grantedFeatChoicePreset`: types.ts:633 already defines `grantedChoiceFeats?: { featId: string; restrictTo?: string[] }[]`, consumed at build.ts:1948-1959 to grant a feat with a restricted sub-choice — the background lane should reuse that shape. Note the hard prerequisite the spec missed: build.ts:1951 does `if (!f?.choice) continue;`, so that lane is inert until feats['multilingual'] gains a language `choice` — which is the real first blocker, exactly as the spec said, just for a different reason.

problem: Self-contradictory, and implementing it literally produces a false/duplicate prompt — the second failure mode the review is meant to catch. It sets needsBuildChoice:true and emits a `choice` with prompt "Granted skill feat" and options labelled "Cat Fall (if you chose Acrobatics)" / "Terrain Expertise (if you chose Survival)", while its own `restriction` states the value "must be derived from backgroundSkillChoice, not asked as a second question". The record already carries trainedSkillChoice:['acrobatics','survival'] and the builder already prompts for it (shared.tsx:2464-2468 → BuildState.backgroundSkillChoice), so a second prompt would ask the player to re-answer a question they just answered, and would let them answer it inconsistently.
correction: needsBuildChoice:false (no new player-facing pick exists; the only pick is the already-modelled skill), needsEngineWork:true.
